content.title: About
content.content: Fruit cocktail in a canned juice pack is a mixture of diced fruits preserved in their own juice. Typical ingredients include peaches, pineapple, pears, oranges and cherries, which are sterilized in a sealed container to retain natural flavor and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canning fruits in their own juice helps retain most of the vitamins, especially vitamin C.
While traditional fruit cocktail was sold in glass jars, modern juice packs are lighter and easier to transport.
In the United States, fruit cocktail is often served in school lunches as a quick source of fruit.
Sugar content varies by brand; some add sweeteners, others rely solely on natural fruit juice.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: The fruit pieces provide soluble and insoluble fiber beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Fruit polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The juice pack adds extra fluid, useful during hot weather.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some varieties contain added sugar, which may be undesirable for people with diabetes or those watching weight.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to specific fruits (e.g., peaches) may react to the cocktail.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain brands use preservatives such as potassium sorbate, which can cause sensitivity in some people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The cocktail can be eaten straight from the pack, mixed into yogurt or oatmeal, or used as a topping for desserts. Give the pack a gentle shake before serving to distribute the juice evenly.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can or pack in a cool, dry place. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.
